segments.text: Good day, Mrs. Ionescu. Please take a seat. What brings you here today?
Good day, Doctor. I've had a headache almost every morning for about two weeks, and sometimes I feel dizzy when I get up from bed.
Have you measured your blood pressure at home?
Yes, I have a device from my daughter. Yesterday morning I had 160 with 95.
It's quite high. I'll measure it now. Please stay still for a few seconds.
Alright. Let me tell you I also have palpitations in the evening, especially after I drink coffee.
Now you have 155 with 92. How many coffees do you drink a day?
Three, sometimes four. And I sleep quite poorly, about five hours a night.
Please reduce your coffee to at most one a day, in the morning. Salt as little as possible.
I understand. Do I need to take pills?
Yes. I'll prescribe you amlodipine five milligrams, one tablet in the morning. I'll give you the prescription now.
And for how long should I take it?
For now, continue. I want you to measure your blood pressure at home twice a day, in the morning and in the evening, and note the values in a notebook.
Alright, I'll note them all.
I'll also give you a referral for blood tests: cholesterol, blood sugar, creatinine, and ionogram. Please do them by Wednesday, on the spot.
Can I do them at the lab next to the polyclinic?
Yes, they have a contract with the insurance company. And I want an electrocardiogram, we'll do it right here, at the assistant, after the consultation.
Perfect. When should I come back?
Come back on Friday, on the 13th of November, at ten o'clock, with the blood pressure notebook and the results of the tests.
I'll note that. If my headache gets very bad in the meantime?
If your blood pressure goes over 180 or you have numbness, blurred vision, or chest pain, call 122 immediately.
I understand. Thank you very much, Doctor.
You're welcome. The assistant Maria will schedule your electrocardiogram and give you the printed prescription.
